summary: Nora now records who said a thing, not just which of her background runs found it.
details: A remembered fact previously recorded only the background run that established it. Nothing anywhere recorded the person who actually claimed it — so three people agreeing and one person repeating themselves were indistinguishable, and there was no way to represent the room disagreeing with itself.

The person is now recovered by joining the messages a claim came from to the sender, entirely inside the database. What she is shown when she reads a batch of chat has not changed: the speaker is still deliberately absent from that prompt, because naming speakers is how a batch of ordinary chat starts looking like a batch of claims about the people in it.
This makes a claim attributable rather than anonymous, which is what a later feature needs to render 'someone told me this' with the someone attached.
Recording who asserted something is not permission to repeat it; what she may say is governed exactly as before.
limitations: A message from someone Nora has not been introduced to has no person behind it, so a claim only they made stays unattributed. That case is counted rather than passed off as 'nobody said it'.
